about:
LGCY Power is based in Newport News, Virginia, and provides residential solar panel options to homeowners in the state and across multiple other states. The company does not disclose its founding year, ownership structure, or founders in the available materials.

The firm operates as a solar installer and service provider, guiding homeowners through a qualification process to determine roof suitability, shading, and utility costs. Its energy consultants then deliver customized monthly savings projections, estimated payoff periods, and financing options. Services include roofing assessment, solar panel installation, system activation, and ongoing customer support for monitoring and troubleshooting.

The primary customers are residential property owners, though the qualification form also accommodates commercial building owners. The company serves the solar energy and residential construction sectors, with a focus on homeowners seeking to reduce utility bills through rooftop solar.

LGCY Power states that it differentiates itself by offering smart, affordable energy solutions and by continuously expanding its geographic footprint. It emphasizes a consultative approach that provides transparent savings estimates and multiple financing pathways.

LKQ Auto Parts of Lincoln operates at 3450 North 35th Circle in Lincoln, Nebraska. The location is part of LKQ Corporation, a national network of automotive salvage and recycled parts facilities. The page does not disclose the founding date of this specific site, nor does it identify individual founders or ownership structure beyond the corporate parent.

The facility functions as a salvage yard and parts distributor, offering used auto body parts, recycled components, remanufactured engines, rebuilt transmissions, and a full line of paint, body, and equipment supplies. Inventory includes radiators, wheels, tires, abrasives, detailing products, and refinish and coating materials. Customers can purchase on-site, arrange local delivery, or have parts shipped via common carriers with tracking. Testimonials on the site reference individual vehicle owners in Lincoln who obtained painted-to-match body panels and mechanical components. The company also lists "Replacement Automotive Labels" and "Keystone Automotive - Lincoln" among its served categories, indicating a mix of trade and consumer channels.

LKQ emphasizes that the bulk of its salvage-yard inventory consists of original equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts installed by the vehicle maker. name: LMI Manufacturing
old_description: LMI's high-precision machining services deliver exact components, meeting even the most rigorous specifications reliably and consistently.
about:
LMI Manufacturing operates from a 40,000-square-foot facility in Hartford, Wisconsin. The company was founded in 1960 on a family farm in the Midwest by Lloyd Luedtke, who invented the Luedke Hay Mover/Hay Conditioner to reduce harvest time for local farmers. After decades of agricultural equipment innovation — including a bale thrower patented for Ford Motors — the business transitioned into a full-scale welding and fabrication shop. In 2018, Ryan Konicek purchased the company and invested in facility renovations and expanded capabilities.

Today LMI provides end-to-end metal fabrication for OEMs nationwide. Core processes include 6 kW fiber laser cutting (up to 79" × 158"), offline-programmed press brake forming, manual and robotic welding certified to 1-inch thickness, CNC milling and turning, and turnkey assembly — all under one roof. The shop also runs turret punching, sawing, grinding, roll forming, and tube bending, with finishing and powder coating coordinated through local partners. A team of roughly 35 employees works across robotic welding cells, CNC machining centers, and precision press brakes.

The company serves OEMs in food processing and packaging (stainless-steel trays, molds, washdown-ready weldments), electrical and power distribution (custom enclosures, lugs, welded assemblies), industrial machinery (large welded frames and system components), data centers (server-room cabinets and hardware), material handling and logistics (conveyor supports, lift-system assemblies, brake components), and agriculture (structural weldments for soil-prep and irrigation equipment). Medical and healthcare customers are also noted.

LMI emphasizes in-house control from laser cutting through final assembly, which shortens lead times and improves traceability. The company reports that 80 percent of quotes are returned within 24–48 hours, and it reserves 20 percent of shop capacity for emergency jobs. Certified welds, QA tracking, and ISO 9001:2015 certification support repeatable quality, while real-time shop-floor dashboards enable accurate lead-time commitments. Average production lead time is two to three weeks, with rush options available.

old_description: We use cookies on our website to give you the most relevant experience by remembering your preferences and repeat visits. By clicking “Accept”, you consent to the use of ALL the cookies.
about:
LS ELECTRIC America is headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois. The business operates as the North American arm of the LS Electric group, which cites more than 50 years of industry experience and a presence in 107 nations. No founding year for the U.S. entity is disclosed, and ownership details such as family or veteran status are not stated in the source material.

The company provides complete low- and medium-voltage power distribution solutions, including transformers, switchgear, switchboards, panelboards, and DC power systems. Its product lineup features the Load Interrupter Switch, Susol UL Smart MCCB, Dead Tank Circuit Breaker, Susol UL ACB, Metal Enclosed Load Interrupter Switchgear, RPP, UL SPD, and Susol UL MCCB (up to 1000 V). Beyond hardware, LS ELECTRIC America runs a Connect Portal for quotes, order tracking, and document management; a Tech Hub with video tutorials and service guides; a Download Center for catalogs and datasheets; and a certified hands-on training program for each product line. The firm emphasizes integrated manufacturing and supply capabilities but does not publish facility size, headcount, or production volumes.

Industries served include data centers, power grid operators, oil and gas, mining, public infrastructure, general industrial, and commercial and residential construction. The company positions its solutions for mission-critical applications such as data centers, manufacturing plants, and commercial infrastructure projects.

LS ELECTRIC America highlights its integrated manufacturing and supply chain, comprehensive warranty coverage across all 50 states, and dedicated engineering and service expertise as key differentiators. Recent press announcements note a VSC-HVDC joint venture with GE Vernova and a European expansion partnership with LS Cable & System, underscoring a focus on next-generation power transmission technology.

old_description: A nationally known and respected manufacturer of work-ready truck and cargo van accessories, including grille guards, running boards and more
about:
Located in Brandon, South Dakota, Plant 141‑A operates as a manufacturing site for LUVERNE, a brand within the Lippert portfolio. Lippert, headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, operates more than 140 facilities worldwide across North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa. The plant runs Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

The facility produces rugged truck accessories such as Grip Steps and rear steps for commercial and fleet vehicles. Its capabilities span metal fabrication, thermoforming, injection molding, coatings, and roto‑molding, supported by on‑site factory service and aftermarket service centers. As part of Lippert’s integrated manufacturing network, the plant leverages shared technology and lean processes.

The plant serves the automotive, RV, marine, commercial transportation, construction, hospitality, and agriculture markets, supplying both OEM and aftermarket customers. Lippert’s brand portfolio includes CURT, Taylor Made, Lewmar, and others, providing components for towing, leveling, slides, and marine applications.

Lippert emphasizes American manufacturing built to withstand tough working conditions, coupled with sustainability initiatives like energy‑efficient systems, waste reduction, and responsible sourcing. The company highlights a culture of employee support and community involvement as part of its operational philosophy.

name: LV Iron & Steel
old_description: Exceptional Iron and Steel Services in Las Vegas for Over 20 Years
about:
LV Iron & Steel is based in Las Vegas, Nevada, and has served the region for more than 20 years. The company does not publish its exact founding date, ownership details, or founder names.

The company provides full-service design, fabrication, and installation of structural and ornamental iron and steel for commercial and residential projects. Its in-house capabilities include robotic plasma cutting (Voortman V807), punching and shearing (Voortman V505), robotic welding (Vectis Cobot), tube plasma cutting (EL-SQRD), high-speed plate processing (Plate Lazer Plus), beam welding, and point-cloud scanning for fit-up. Services span steel fabrication, design-assist, BIM modeling and detailing, complex coating management, and steel erection. Residential products include custom gates, fences, carports, patio covers, security doors, and wrought iron doors. Fabrication lead times for custom residential work run 4–6 weeks.

LV Iron & Steel works with general contractors, architects, and developers on commercial projects such as superstructures and custom homes. It also serves homeowners directly in the Las Vegas area, including communities like Summerlin, Henderson, North Las Vegas, and Boulder City.

The firm emphasizes proactive communication, safety-first practices, and seamless coordination with other trades to keep projects on schedule and within budget. Its in-house fabrication process is cited as the foundation for strict quality control across all work.

name: Laborie Medical Technologies
old_description: Advancing Gastrointestinal Health through Diagnostic and Therapeutic Solutions
about:
Laborie Medical Technologies is headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The company was founded in 1967 by Ray Laborie, a pioneer in urodynamics. It is privately owned by Patricia Industries, a division of the Investor AB network, which takes a long-term investment approach.

Laborie designs, manufactures, and delivers diagnostic and therapeutic medical devices for urology, urogynecology, gastroenterology, and maternal & child health. Its product portfolio includes the Optilume BPH Catheter System, the Eclipse System for bowel control, the LifeBubble umbilical catheter securement system, and the Solar Compact System for anorectal manometry. The company employs over 1,000 people worldwide and has grown through a series of strategic acquisitions since 2006.

The company serves clinicians and hospitals across gastroenterology, urology, urogynecology, obstetrics, gynecology, neonatology, and colorectal specialties. Its solutions are used in diagnostic procedures such as urodynamics, anorectal manometry, and pharyngeal manometry, as well as in therapeutic interventions for benign prostatic hyperplasia, fecal incontinence, and postpartum hemorrhage.

Laborie states that its mission is to operate as a specialist medical company that makes and advances technologies to preserve and restore human dignity. It differentiates itself through market-expertise in its specialty areas and a Clinical Education & Information Program that supports its products with training and resources.
